---
title: Styles
description: One Tailwind build for the app, and a separate theme for the admin.

An app that uses Pluto has exactly one Tailwind build. The CSS entry of the app owns it. No Pluto layer registers a Tailwind entry of its own.

## Why

If two Tailwind builds are in one page, they declare the same cascade layers. A utility from the later stylesheet overrides the same utility of the earlier one. The responsive layout of the admin then breaks.

## The CSS entry

Start your CSS entry with these three imports. Add your own theme after them.

```css [app/assets/css/main.css]
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@nuxt/ui';
@import '#build/pluto.css';

@theme {
  /* your site's tokens */
}
```

Register the file in `nuxt.config.ts`:

```ts [nuxt.config.ts]
export default defineNuxtConfig({
  css: ['~/assets/css/main.css']
})
```

`#build/pluto.css` brings in the CSS of every Pluto layer, including the admin theme. Nuxt UI already scans the source of every layer.

## The `pluto-css` module

The module `pluto-css` is part of core. It does these things:

1. It finds the `pluto-layer.css` file of every layer.
2. It writes `#build/pluto.css`, which imports each layer file. The base layer comes first, so a higher layer wins.
3. It writes a fallback entry.
4. It reads your CSS entries. If none imports `tailwindcss`, it adds the fallback entry. This keeps a layer repository that runs on its own styled.

The module has one option, `plutoCss.check`. The default is `true`. Set it to `false` to turn the warnings off. The module prints nothing during `nuxt prepare`.

The build prints a `pluto-css` warning, once for each problem, when:

- A layer registers its own Tailwind build.
- More than one Tailwind build exists.
- No entry imports `#build/pluto.css`.
- No entry imports `@nuxt/ui`.

The module does not add a second build when your app forgets the import.

## Rules for a layer

A layer can ship `app/assets/css/pluto-layer.css`.

- Never import `tailwindcss` or `@nuxt/ui` in it.
- Use only `@theme`, `@custom-variant`, `@utility`, unlayered rules, and imports of plain CSS files next to it.
- Add no `@source` for the `app/` directory of the layer.
- Register no `css` entry in the `nuxt.config` of the layer.

## Check the build

In the browser console, count the Tailwind builds:

```js
[...document.querySelectorAll('style[data-vite-dev-id]')].filter(s => s.textContent.includes('tailwindcss v4')).length
```

The result must be 1, on the admin and on the public site. The build log must have no `pluto-css` warning.

## The admin theme

The admin has its own look. Your `app.config` colors and `@theme` tokens do not change it.

| Role | Color |
| --- | --- |
| primary | indigo |
| secondary | violet |
| success | green |
| info | blue |
| warning | amber |
| error | red |
| neutral | zinc |

The admin font is Outfit. The admin radius is `0.25rem`.

The theme applies under two selectors:

- `:root[data-pluto-admin]`. The composable `usePlutoAdminTheme()` sets `data-pluto-admin` on `<html>` while an admin layout is mounted. Overlays such as modals and menus also get the theme.
- `[data-pluto-admin-scope]`. It is for admin chrome that shows on the public site, such as the navbar of a signed-in admin.

Every value is a literal OKLCH color, so an app cannot redefine it.

### Surfaces

In dark mode, the surfaces go from the darkest at the top to the lightest in the content: navbar, sidebar, canvas, cards. The navbar is near black in both modes.

### The admin bar height

The token `--pluto-admin-bar-height` is `2.5rem` on `:root`. A public site can use it to offset its own header under the admin bar. `PlutoRoot` sets `data-pluto-admin-bar` on `<html>` while the bar shows. See [Admin shell](/core/admin-shell#offset-your-own-header).

### Rules for admin code

- Use Nuxt UI semantic classes such as `bg-default`, `text-muted`, and `border-default`. Do not use raw Tailwind colors such as `bg-zinc-100`. Raw colors do not follow the admin theme.
- Call `usePlutoAdminTheme()` in every new admin layout.
- Put `data-pluto-admin-scope` on admin chrome that renders outside an admin layout.
- Never put the admin radius in `@theme`. It would reach the public site.

::note
Component themes in `app.config`, such as `ui.button.slots.base`, still merge across layers and reach the admin. Only colors, tokens, surfaces, and the font are isolated.
::
